candidate_sources.README.md:
# Rail timetable lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Java query objects and observer handles; per-attempt completion and real abort adapter

boolean active(Query q,Attempt a){return q.attempt==a&&!a.settled;}
if(q.observers.isEmpty()){Attempt a=q.attempt;if(a!=null&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}
void resume(Query q){Attempt a=q.attempt;if(a!=null&&active(q,a)&&q.state.get("fetchStatus").equals("paused")&&eligible(a)&&!a.queued){a.queued=true;

int token=env.bind(x->{a.queued=false;if(!active(q,a))return null;if(a.failures>0&&a.retryCancelled){a.settled=true;q.state.put("status","error");q.state.put("fetchStatus","idle");return null;}invoke(q,a);return null;});env.call("defer",token);
if(!options.getOrDefault("networkMode","online").equals("online")||online)invoke(q,a);else q.state.put("fetchStatus","paused");

No original source supports a behavioral contract revision. The previous candidate adds a started distinction and cancels a never-started attempt, which is directionally consistent with the contract, but the opaque failed acceptance verdict neither identifies a remaining defect nor creates a new requirement.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract remains supported by the original task and public README/source and needs no revision. The previous candidate appears to address the stated lifecycle hole by recording request entry, canceling a final-observer attempt that has not started, and rechecking permission both when scheduling and when running a deferred resume. It also retains active unconsumed work after observer departure. The supplied compilation observation establishes syntax only, while the unexplained failed acceptance verdict does not identify a source-grounded behavioral violation. Therefore neither a specific implementation gap nor a contract gap can be established from the permitted evidence.

routing_analysis.contract: A fresh online-mode attempt created while offline must not enter its signal-consuming request with a live signal after its final observer departs before execution, including across an already queued deferred resume and regardless of refetchOnReconnect. Observer departure must invalidate or cancel that attempt before request entry; resume and completion must revalidate native attempt identity. Preserve synchronous eligible entry, asynchronous focused continuation, network modes, retry scheduling, shared fetches, cache persistence, completion of already-entered unconsumed work, physical abort of consumed work, cancellation rollback, public interfaces, dependencies, and configuration.
